A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DRAG/IterDRAG study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching content across the changed appendix numbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original question-answering experiments, retrieval evaluations, computation-allocation ablations and generalization tests, including Tables 1–8 and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds an experiment using GTR XXL on MuSiQue in Appendix D and Figure 10.

M1.justification: DRAG, IterDRAG and the computation allocation model retain their procedures and formulation. GTR XXL is tested as an alternative retrieval configuration; no new algorithmic component or inference procedure is introduced.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Bamboogle, HotpotQA, MuSiQue, 2WikiMultiHopQA, TriviaQA, Natural Questions and StrategyQA. The added experiment reuses MuSiQue with another retriever and a smaller sample, without extending dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The zero-shot QA, many-shot QA, RAG, CoT and allocation-model baseline/oracle comparisons are retained. New Figure 10 again compares RAG, DRAG and IterDRAG; GTR XXL supplies retrieval rather than serving as an additional competing RAG method.

E3.justification: New Appendix D introduces an additional configuration using GTR XXL with Gemini 1.5 Flash on 100 sampled MuSiQue examples. The existing experiments retain their reported retrieval configuration, metrics, context budgets and parameter sweeps.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds a focused robustness check asking whether the scaling trends persist with a different retriever. Existing ablations, parameter analyses, generalization and extrapolation tests, and error cases are retained.

E5.justification: The coefficient significance reporting in Table 8 and existing statistical reporting remain unchanged. The GTR experiment introduces no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or additional significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: New Figure 10 reports normalized performance curves showing RAG saturation and continued scaling benefits for DRAG/IterDRAG under GTR XXL. These are additional results under a different configuration, not same-setting improvements over v1. Existing numerical tables and findings are retained.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(2), the informativeness definitions and allocation-model mathematics are retained. Explicitly stating that a and b are three-dimensional vectors and c is scalar clarifies existing notation without changing the mathematical formulation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about DRAG/IterDRAG, near-linear scaling with orders of magnitude of compute, allocation prediction and gains up to 58.9%. The abstract's revised emphasis on combining strategies does not change their substance.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds an explicit interpretation of the compute–performance trade-off as depending primarily on available budget under optimal allocation. Appendix D interprets the GTR results as supporting generality across retrievers. Existing retrieval, reasoning and long-context limitations remain.

D1.justification: The added experiment specifies the GTR XXL retriever, Gemini 1.5 Flash generator and 100-example sample, providing limited reproducibility information for that check. The implementation appendix and prompt templates otherwise retain their details, with no new code or data access instructions.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Leng et al. on long-context RAG, Yue et al. on evidence-driven retrieval-augmented generation, and Ni et al. for GTR. These are limited additions; the overall research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized wording and citation corrections, a revised abstract sentence, an expanded trade-off discussion and an inserted appendix subsection. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 10 and restyles Figure 7 with different colors, markers, dashed lines, gridlines and axis scaling. Existing appendix figures and Table 8 are repositioned, with subsequent figures renumbered; the overall document design is retained.

improvement.justification: The GTR XXL experiment adds useful evidence that the scaling observation extends beyond v1's Gecko-1B retriever, while preserving existing results. This is a limited gain because it covers only 100 MuSiQue examples. The new discussion's wording about steady gains is also less qualified than the retained finding of diminishing gains beyond 1M tokens.
